commit.message:
fix(history): keep truncation markers from forcing a collapse

A record whose unmarked wire form fits the 64 KiB budget could be pushed
over it by the marker bytes alone and collapse to a stub. A tool result
carrying an MCP App block lost that block purely because a sibling list
was trimmed and marked.

Measure the unmarked form when the marked one overflows and serve it as is
when it fits: the record keeps its data and the MCP App block survives,
while markers stay in place everywhere the budget allows them.

fix(history): mark list and depth truncation on the wire

The history sanitizer trimmed lists to 100 items and replaced anything past
depth 8 with "<truncated>" without telling anyone, so a reopened session
showed structured fields that no longer matched the record on disk.

Stamp the owning mapping with <key>_truncated and the record with
truncated: true. A pre-set falsy flag is upgraded; a pre-set truthy one
(e.g. raw_output_truncated from the live rail) is kept as is. Arrays stay
arrays so the frontend's Array.isArray guards keep rendering the prefix,
and strings keep their visible " [truncated]" suffix.

The MCP App block is excluded from the stats because it is restored
byte-for-byte afterwards: its own lists and depth must not mark the record
or push a near-budget record into the collapse path.
